title: A failed Kokoro install starts over from byte zero of all 374 MB
body:
## Summary
A Kokoro install that fails or is interrupted keeps nothing: the next press downloads the 24 MB engine and the 350 MB model again from the start, and nothing is resumed.

## Description
`Installer._kokoro` (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:358-369) downloads both archives into a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` and extracts only after both have arrived, so a model failure discards an engine that had arrived whole. `_fetch` opens its destination `wb` and sends no `Range` (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:430), so a download cut at 300 of 350 MB restarts at 0. `start` always opens Kokoro at `downloading_engine` (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:297-300), unlike the whisper half, which skips an engine already present (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:375). A daemon killed mid-run also leaves the temp directory behind in %TEMP%. voice-io / voice-setup-experience rule 2 asks for a resumable step: closing the window halfway resumes at that step. Fixed looks like: the engine extracted (and verified) before the model download starts, a present and running engine skipped, and the model fetched into a `.partial` in the engine home that a retry resumes with `Range`, re-hashing the kept prefix against the pin.

## Flow
- Install Kokoro; the model download fails at 300 of 350 MB (a dropped Wi-Fi)
- -> `_download` deletes the partial, the TemporaryDirectory deletes the engine archive -> state `failed`
- Press Install again -> `downloading_engine` from 0, then the model from 0
- Build order: staged extract, skip a running engine, `.partial` + `Range` resume with the hash seeded from the kept bytes, a cleanup of stale `.partial` files

## Expected impact
A person on a slow or flaky link who retries after a failure; measured as bytes fetched by the retry. Could break: a server that ignores `Range` (answers 200) must restart cleanly, and the SHA-256 pin must cover the joined bytes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a retry fetches only what the failed run did not keep
Before: by reading the code, a retry after a model failure at 300 of 350 MB fetches 24.4 + 349.9 MB (the whole run again)
After: predicted 49.9 MB (the model's missing tail), 0 for the engine
Method: simulation - three cases walked (model fails mid-way; engine fails; daemon killed mid-model); the test server in tests/channels/test_voice_install.py serves no Range, so no figure could be taken this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:360 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(...)
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:363-364 both downloads before any extract
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:368 extract_sherpa_engine(engine_tar, bin_dir)
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:430 with dest.open("wb") as out:  (no Range)
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:297-300 kokoro always opens downloading_engine
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:375 whisper: if whisper.engine_path(...) is None
instrument: Give the test server in tests/channels/test_voice_install.py Range support and a per-path byte counter; fail the model mid-body once; compare bytes fetched by the retry on both arms (before: engine + whole model; after: the model's tail only).

title: Install answers not_needed for an engine the studio's probe calls broken
body:
## Summary
When every Kokoro file is present but the engine will not run, the studio says "Kokoro's engine will not run" and its Install answers `not_needed`, so the one repair the studio offers does nothing; whisper's install skips a present-but-broken engine the same way.

## Description
`Installer._installed` (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:309-319) decides `not_needed` by file presence only (`kokoro.paths_for(...).missing()`, `whisper.engine_path(...) is not None`), while the studio's readiness is `kokoro.probe` / `whisper.probe`, which also runs the executable (src/athena/channels/voice/home.py dry_check). Two renderings of "is it installed" that disagree on exactly the broken state. For whisper, `_whisper` also skips the engine download whenever a file is there (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:375), so even a model install would not repair the engine, and the files-only verify would report `completed`. voice-io / engine-abstraction: absent and broken are different facts, and the action offered must fit the one reported. Fixed looks like: the start decision asks the probe (outside the installer lock, since it may spawn), a broken engine is re-fetched, and the verify after extraction says `failed` with the probe's reason when the new engine still will not run.

## Flow
- Personas left a Kokoro tree whose engine is missing a DLL
- Voice studio -> Kokoro `broken`, reason "will not run ... exited with -1073741515" -> press Install
- -> `Installer.start` -> `_installed` -> files all present -> `not_needed`
- -> nothing downloads; the studio still says broken; the only way out is by hand

## Expected impact
A person whose engine tree is damaged (a partial Personas install, an antivirus quarantine of a DLL); measured as whether Install leaves the probe `ready`. Could break: the tests' fake engines are not runnable executables, so the verify needs an injected probe; and a repair that cannot fix a missing system runtime must say so rather than loop.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Install repairs the broken state the studio reports
Before: probe on a home with every Kokoro file and a non-runnable sherpa-onnx-offline-tts.exe: `kokoro.probe` = broken ("would not start (OSError)"), `Installer(homes, platform="win32").start("kokoro")` = `not_needed` (run this round, scratch home)
After: predicted - start proceeds to `downloading_engine`, and the run ends `completed` only when the probe is ready, else `failed` with its reason
Method: probe for Before; After walked, not built - the fix touches start, the whisper engine skip and the verify, and needs runnable fakes or injected probes in tests/channels/test_voice_install.py (M, risk 4)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe (2026-10-16, scratch home):
probe: EngineProbe(state='broken', reason="Kokoro's engine will not run: sherpa-onnx-offline-tts.exe would not start (OSError).")
install: InstallState(component='kokoro', state='not_needed', ...)
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:294-296 if self._installed(...): not_needed
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:313 return not kokoro.paths_for(self.homes).missing()
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:375 if whisper.engine_path(self.homes) is None:
src/athena/channels/voice/kokoro.py:184-187 the probe runs dry_check
instrument: tests/channels/test_voice_install.py: a home with every file and an injected probe that says broken; assert start() does not answer not_needed and the run ends completed only once the probe says ready (and failed with its reason otherwise); the same for whisper with a present engine and model.

title: An install lock left by a killed daemon blocks every install for an hour
body:
## Summary
A daemon stopped or killed mid-install leaves `.install.lock` in the engine home, and every Install press for the next hour fails with "another install is writing".

## Description
The install runs on a daemon thread (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:304) and the lock is removed only by `_HomeLock.__exit__`, which a killed or exiting process never runs; nothing in the daemon's shutdown joins the installer (no caller outside config.py and daemon/voice.py). `_HomeLock.__enter__` treats any lock younger than STALE_LOCK_S, one hour (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:97, :477), as held, although the lock it wrote names its owner and pid (src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:485). The person who closed the app during a download and reopened it is told Personas or another Athena is installing. voice-io / voice-setup-experience: a failure mid-download must not read as voice not working. Fixed looks like: a lock whose owner is athena and whose pid is not a live process is stale at once (checked with OpenProcess and GetExitCodeProcess on Windows, never `os.kill(pid, 0)`, which sends CTRL_C_EVENT there).

## Flow
- Press Install Kokoro; close the window during the model download (the shell stops the daemon)
- Reopen; press Install -> `_HomeLock.__enter__` finds a 5-minute-old lock
- -> InstallError "another install is writing companion-tts (Personas or another Athena); try again when it finishes" -> `failed`, for up to an hour

## Expected impact
Anyone who quits mid-install; measured as whether a retry after a killed run starts. Could break: pid reuse could make a dead owner look alive (the fallback is the hour it waits today), and a lock written by Personas carries Personas' own shape.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a retry after a killed run starts at once
Before: by reading the code, a lock with a dead pid younger than 3600 s fails the run with "another install is writing"
After: predicted - the same lock with a dead athena pid is taken over and the run starts; a live pid or a foreign owner still refuses
Method: simulation - three cases walked (killed Athena, live Personas, pid reused); a test needs a dead pid (a child process that has exited) and a stdlib liveness check per platform, not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:97 STALE_LOCK_S = 60 * 60.0
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:304 Thread(..., name="voice-install", daemon=True)
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:477-481 if age < STALE_LOCK_S: raise InstallError("another install is writing ...")
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:485 json.dump({"owner": "athena", "pid": os.getpid(), ...})
git grep -n installer -- src (outside install.py): config.py and daemon/voice.py only; no shutdown join
instrument: tests/channels/test_voice_install.py: write a lock naming owner athena and the pid of a child process that has already exited, age 60 s; before: the run fails with "another install is writing"; after: it completes. A second case with the test's own live pid must still refuse.

title: The desktop's typed voice path (useVoice.say) has no production caller
body:
## Summary
The gateway's `text` frame is a live, tested server path, but its only desktop sender, `useVoice.say` in apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts, is called by tests and nothing else; `VoiceSession.say` is not part of the question, it is the gateway's own speaker queue with two in-tree callers.

## Description
Backlog item from the 2026-10-15 challenge run, judged on the current tree. `VoiceSession.say` (src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:698) is the speaker's enqueue, called by `_turn` (src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:947) and `_answer` (src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:1015); a desktop caller of it is not a thing that could exist, so that half of the item is false. The typed `text` frame (src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:514, documented at :12-13 "for a client with no microphone") is not dead: tests/channels/test_voice_gateway.py sends it 37 times and apps/desktop/src/lib/voice.ts:165 declares it. On the desktop, `useVoice.say` (apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:527, typed at :136-137 "for a test or a keyboard fallback") has zero callers outside stores/voice.test.ts. So it is a missing caller, and whether the desktop wants a keyboard fallback on the voice channel - the typed companion already reaches the lane through the run route - is a product call in another context. voice-io golden path: a spoken command channel that is down must leave every command reachable, which the run route already does.

## Flow
- grep apps/desktop/src for a non-test caller of useVoice.getState().say or the store's say -> none
- Options for the owner: wire a keyboard fallback that sends the `text` frame (a desktop card), or delete `useVoice.say` and its tests and keep the server frame for scripted clients

## Expected impact
Desktop maintainers; a decision removes either an unused store method or an unbuilt affordance. Could break: nothing until one is chosen.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the typed voice path is either used or gone on the desktop
Before: production callers of useVoice.say in apps/desktop/src: 0 (tests: 6 calls in stores/voice.test.ts); server `text` frame: tested, documented
After: 1 caller, or the method removed - depends on the owner's call
Method: probe - the zero-consumer grep below; the After is a direction, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rn "say(" apps/desktop/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx (excluding *.test.ts): no caller of the voice store's say; the hits are companion/machine.ts and scenes/chores say props, unrelated
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:136 /** The typed path of the same channel, for a test or a keyboard fallback. */
apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.test.ts:262,273,283,316,344,356 the only callers
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:947, :1015 the two callers of VoiceSession.say

title: A sealed OpenAI key that cannot be read is reported as no key at all
body:
## Summary
When the sealed voice key exists but will not unseal, the studio says "No OpenAI key is set", because the seal answers `None` for a missing and an unreadable key alike.

## Description
`FileSeal.unseal` (src/athena/connectors/seal.py:107-114) returns `None` both when the file is missing and when decoding fails (`except (OSError, ValueError): return None`, which covers a DPAPI refusal after a profile move). `VoiceStudio.openai_key` (src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:357-363) then falls through to the environment and `probe_openai` (src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:233-239) reports `absent` with "No OpenAI key is set". voice-io / engine-abstraction: absent and broken are different facts. Fixed looks like: the seal port distinguishes unreadable from missing (a connectors-context change), and the studio says the stored key could not be read and asks for it again.

## Flow
- Seal a key; the sealed file later fails to decode (DPAPI refuses it)
- Open the voice studio -> `probe_openai` -> "No OpenAI key is set; add one"
- The person who set one is told they did not

## Expected impact
Cloud-listener users after a machine or profile change; the remedy (paste the key again) already works, so only the sentence misleads. Could break: the seal port is shared with connectors.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the studio names an unreadable key as unreadable
Before: by reading the code, one sentence for both states
After: predicted two sentences, one per state
Method: simulation - the seal lives in connectors (not this round's paths), so no probe was built against it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/connectors/seal.py:107-114 unseal: missing -> None; (OSError, ValueError) -> None
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:360-363 sealed or environ
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:238 "No OpenAI key is set; add one in the voice studio to transcribe in the cloud."
instrument: tests/channels/test_voice_config.py with a seal stub whose unseal raises an unreadable error (needs the connectors SealPort to grow that distinction): before the view's openai reason is "No OpenAI key is set", after it names the unreadable key.
